messages:
zara: Heads up — after last night's kernel-selector tweak we're seeing a Mixtral MoE regression in prod. router p99 up ~15% and KV cache evictions spiked.
ashwin: yep, noticed on the perf dashboard. evictions/s went from ~300 -> ~950 on the busiest pods. interestingly only Mixtral pools, not Llama or Qwen.
ben: do we have a short profiler dump? I want to see which kernel variant is being chosen for the router + FFN paths.
claire: reproducer suggestion: run a short loadtest with seq=512 and a realistic prompt mix. I used `./tools/loadtest --model mixtral-9b --qps 180 --seq 512 --duration 60s --tag kernel-debug` locally and it surfaced the same p99 jump.
zara: here's a trimmed profile from one affected pod (sensitive bits removed):
```
runtime_profile.v2:
- router_latency_ms: p50=12 p95=46 p99=122
- kv_cache_evictions_per_s: 310 -> 980
- kernel_selection: matmul::fast_gemm_v2 (FFN) ; router_matmul -> generic_fp32_fallback
- expert_remote_bytes/s: +28% vs baseline
- batching: avg_batch_size=9.1 (target 8), batch_window_ms=5
```
ashwin: that `generic_fp32_fallback` for router_matmul is suspicious. we pushed a heuristic that prefers quantized fused kernels for FFN but left router kernel rules loose — could be choosing an incompatible kernel causing slower code path and bigger working set.
ben: quick experiment: toggled `--kernel-selector=strict-v1` on a canary and also set `--router-temp=0.9` and `--expert-parallelism=1`.
ben: results after 10m canary: p99 down from 122 -> 96 ms, remote expert traffic down ~18%, kv evictions dropped ~25%.
claire: promising. do we think RoPE scaling or head/kv dim mismatch amplified this? Mixtral has nonstandard head dims and we've seen RoPE scaling affect cache locality before.
az:
zara: I suspect two compounding factors: (1) kernel selector picked a slower generic kernel for router matmul (more memory thrash), (2) scheduler packing changed effective head distribution causing more cross-expert calls -> cache pressure.
ashwin: agree. also saw that after quantization tweak (int8 path) the kernel selector rules mapped FFN -> fused_s8 but router path missed the mapping because of shape variance (num_heads * head_dim not aligned), so fallback.
ben: mitigation ideas:
- tighten kernel-selector rules for router_matmul shapes (force fused path when dims align)
- add a router-specific batching heuristic: prefer smaller micro-batches to reduce remote fanout
- enable head_affinity heuristic to bias routing to local experts
- temporarily lower router temperature and raise top_k threshold to reduce noisy routing
claire: can we test `head_affinity=true` + `batch_window_ms=8` + `router_temp=0.8` in a controlled A/B? ben, can you run that against the same loadtest.
ben: running now. command I used:
```
./tools/loadtest --model mixtral-9b --qps 180 --seq 512 --duration 120s \
  --flags 'head_affinity=true,batch_window_ms=8,router_temp=0.8' --tag affinity-test
```
ben: 2m in — early numbers: remote expert traffic -22%, p99 ~100ms. kv evictions trending down. will post full after 120s.
ben: done. summary:
```
affinity-test summary:
- p50=11 p95=42 p99=99 (baseline canary p99=122)
- remote_expert_bytes/s -22%
- kv_evictions/s -30%
- avg_batch_size=7.8
```
zara: sweet. seems head_affinity + small batch_window trades slight throughput for big latency and cache wins.
ashwin: next steps: 1) roll kernel-selector strict-v1 to all mixtral canaries, 2) enable head_affinity by default for Mixtral pools, 3) add a defensive rule in selector to avoid generic_fp32 fallback for router shapes (emit a warning + telemetry). I'll open PRs for 1 & 3.
claire: also schedule an overnight A/B with 5% traffic on real production to validate no hidden regressions. I'll create the experiment and alert if kv_evictions spike.
infra-bot: deploy job started: canary/selector-strict-v1 -> eng-runtime-mixtral-canary-3 (job id abc123)
zara: thanks all — great triage. please paste PR links and the experiment id when ready.
